issues.description: Method Stock.findStockIngredient: The problem statement UML and the solution repository define a method findStockIngredient(String) (single String parameter) returning StockIngredient, and example usage in Main calls findStockIngredient("Bacon") with a single argument. The template repository's Stock class instead defines findStockIngredient(String name, boolean caseSensitive) (two parameters). This parameter-list mismatch between the template and both the problem statement and solution will confuse students and may cause code that uses the single-argument version (as shown in the example Main) to fail to compile or require non-obvious changes.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template Stock API match the problem statement and solution. Add a single-parameter overload: public StockIngredient findStockIngredient(String name) that delegates to the existing two-parameter implementation (for example: return findStockIngredient(name, false);), or replace the two-parameter method with the single-parameter version and, if needed, provide a separate case-sensitive variant. Also ensure the example usage in Main and any documentation refer to the single-parameter method.

issues.description: Concept: method to locate a StockIngredient by its name. Problem statement / UML and the provided solution define a single-argument method named findStockIngredient(String). Template: the Stock class only declares findStockIngredient(String name, boolean caseSensitive) (two parameters). This naming/signature mismatch means the conceptual operation 'find stock ingredient by name' is represented by different method signatures across artifacts: problem/solution expect findStockIngredient(String), template exposes findStockIngredient(String, boolean). A student following the UML or solution will try to call stock.findStockIngredient(name) and encounter a missing-method compile error or be forced to introduce the extra boolean argument. The unexpected 'caseSensitive' parameter increases extraneous cognitive load and can block straightforward implementation of SealSaloon methods that rely on the single-argument API.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template's API match the UML/solution. Option A (non-breaking, recommended): add a single-argument overload in the template: public StockIngredient findStockIngredient(String name) { return findStockIngredient(name, true); } Option B: change the template method signature to public StockIngredient findStockIngredient(String name) and implement case-sensitive lookup (e.g., use equals). Either change aligns the template with the problem statement and solution and removes the unexpected 'caseSensitive' parameter that confuses students.
